paragraphs: Atlas Energy Solutions Inc. is a leading proppant producer, logistics, and distributed power solutions provider, primarily serving the Permian Basin of West Texas and New Mexico. We operate our business through two reportable segments: Sand and Logistics and Power. Our mission is to improve human beings' access to the hydrocarbons that power our lives, and, by doing so, we maximize the value creation for our stockholders. Value creation for our shareholders is our fundamental goal. In order to fulfill our mission and create value for our shareholders, we strive to optimize the outcomes for our broader stakeholders, including our employees and the communities in which we operate. We are proud of the fact that our approach to innovation in the hydrocarbon industry drives efficiencies creating value for our shareholders, while also delivering differentiated social and environmental progress. The Company has driven innovation designed to provide industry-leading environmental benefits by reducing energy consumption, emissions, and our aerial footprint. We call this Sustainable Environmental and Social Progress, and it is driven by shareholder value creation.

We were founded in 2017 by Ben M. "Bud" Brigham, our Executive Chairman, and are led by an entrepreneurial team with a history of constructive disruption bringing significant and complementary experience to this enterprise, including the perspective of longtime E&P operators, which provides for an elevated understanding of the end users of our products and services. Our executive management team has a proven track record with a history of generating positive returns and value creation. Our experience as E&P operators was instrumental to our understanding of the opportunity created by in-basin sand production and supply in the Permian Basin, which we view as North America's premier shale resource and which we believe will remain its most active through economic cycles.

We operate 14 proppant production facilities across the Permian Basin including both large-scale in-basin facilities and smaller distributed mining units. We are a low-cost producer of various high-quality, locally sourced proppants used during the well completion process. We offer both dry and damp sand and carry various mesh sizes including 100 mesh and 40/70 mesh. Proppant is a key component necessary to facilitate the recovery of hydrocarbons from oil and natural gas wells. We operate a differentiated logistics platform that is designed to increase the efficiency, safety and sustainability of the oil and natural gas industry primarily within the Permian Basin. This includes our fleet of fit-for-purpose trucks, trailers, wellsite equipment, and the 42-mile Dune Express conveyor system (the only proppant conveyor system in the world, and the longest conveyor in the United States). We are also integrating autonomous driving technologies in certain of our fit-for-purpose trucks, creating the first semi-autonomous oilfield logistics network to increase the automation of the oil and gas proppant supply chain.

We provide distributed power solutions through a fleet of natural gas-powered reciprocating generators primarily supporting production and artificial lift operations across major United States resource basins. Our generators are designed for heavy-duty, harsh environments for mission critical power needs. Our in-house manufacturing and remanufacturing capabilities, coupled with critical in-field service, provide quality control and standardization across the fleet ensuring market-leading uptime.

Our Kermit facilities, Monahans facility, and OnCore distributed mining network are located in West Texas. The Kermit facilities consist of the two internally developed Kermit facilities ("K1/K2") and the two facilities acquired in the Hi-Crush Transaction ("K115/874"). The facilities and OnCore distributed mining network encompass 45,855 gross acres in the aggregate that we own or lease. We have substantial off-dune acreage at Monahans that is not included in our estimated reserves or resources but that could be mined following our removal of material, such as soil and unusable sand, that lies above the useable sand and must be removed to excavate the useable sand, which we refer to as "overburden."

The Dune Express, which originates at our Kermit facilities and stretches into the middle of the Northern Delaware Basin, is the first long-haul proppant conveyor system in the world. The Dune Express is 42 miles in length, capable of transporting 13 million tons of proppant annually, and is strategically located to deliver proppant to the Northern Delaware Basin. The Dune Express has lowered legacy transportation requirements and increased safety by removing trucks from public roadways, thus reducing traffic, accidents and fatalities on public roadways in the region.

We installed two permanent loadout facilities, one located on the Texas side of the Texas-New Mexico state line approximately at the midpoint of the conveyor and one located at the end of the Dune Express right-of-way on BLM land near the Lea-Eddy County line in New Mexico. The conveyor system also utilizes one or more mobile offload systems, which can be mobilized and relocated from time to time, to maximize delivery efficiencies for customers that are proximate to the conveyor system but not proximate to one of the two permanent loadouts connected to the system.

Our distributed power solutions include a fleet of more than 1,000 natural gas-powered reciprocating generators, with power generation primarily supporting production and artificial lift operations across major United States resource basins.

On November 2, 2025, Atlas LLC entered into a reservation agreement (the "Reservation Agreement") for the manufacture of approximately 240 megawatts of power generation equipment. The aggregate cost of such equipment is approximately $278.3 million. The Reservation Agreement was assigned to Stonebriar in connection with entry into the Lease Documents. The cost of the investment will be financed under the Lease Documents as progress payments become due. We expect deliveries of the equipment to begin in late-2026. Pursuant to the Reservation Agreement, the parties agreed to negotiate and enter into an engineering, procurement and construction agreement governing the terms of the manufacture, delivery and installation of the equipment, which is expected to contain customary representations, warranties and agreements of the parties, indemnification obligations and other customary terms and conditions associated therewith.
The following map shows the locations of our operations as of December 31, 2025: Sand and Logistics

The Kermit facilities and the Monahans facility were built to produce high quality 40/70-mesh and 100-mesh sands, each of which is used extensively in upstream operations in the Permian Basin. Innovative plant design and large-scale operations facilitate low-cost operations and continuity on site. Redundancies were designed into our facilities to remove singular points of failure that could disrupt the production process, ensuring maximum reliability of proppant production and delivery. The facilities are capable of operating year-round and feature advanced safety designs, onsite water supply, power infrastructure and access to low-cost natural gas through connections to interstate natural gas lines. Our OnCore distributed mining network is comprised of 9, built-for-purpose mobile processing plants which produce wet (i.e., undried or damp) 100-mesh sand from leased or customer-owned properties. At each OnCore site, we are responsible for mining and processing the raw sand, selling the finished frac sand products, and reclaiming the disturbed land. The mobility of the OnCore plants provides a great deal of flexibility not afforded to large-scale fixed-plant mining operations.

Further, we benefit from the strategic locations of our facilities, proximal to major highways at the south and north ends of the Winkler Sand Trend. Our Kermit facilities are bisected by two state highways, while our Monahans facility its adjacent to two highways, one of which is Interstate 20, facilitating efficient transportation of our proppant to customers located at various points within the Permian Basin. Accessibility to the western sites for the OnCore mines is via Texas state highway TX-302 or U.S. Route 285; while primary access to the eastern sites is via Interstate 20, state highways TX-137, TX-176, or TX-349.

The operations of our sand facilities are managed and monitored in a highly automated manner from our command center in Austin, Texas. The remote ecosystem allows our employees to simultaneously manage processes at all facilities, resulting in personnel productivity gains.

Our differentiated logistics platform operates primarily within the Permian Basin. This includes our fleet of fit-for-purpose trucks, trailers, wellsite equipment, and the 42-mile Dune Express conveyor system.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Operations
Our business operations depend on the level of activity in the oil and natural gas industries, which experience substantial volatility.
Our business is subject to the cyclical nature of our customers' businesses and the oil and natural gas and power industry.
Decreased demand for proppant or the development of technically- and cost-effective alternative proppants or new processes to replace hydraulic fracturing would negatively impact our business.
The carrying value of our property, plant and equipment ("PP&E") is subject to impairment charges.
Our distributed power segment is dependent on its relationships with key suppliers to obtain equipment for its business.
Many of our power systems involve long sales cycles.
Our customers may not continue to outsource their power system needs.
Distributed power solutions in some applications compete with access to the grid.
We expect our power segment to face significant competition in the future as the mobile power industry evolves.
Operation of power generation facilities involves significant risks and hazards customary to the power industry, which we cannot assure our insurance will be adequate to cover.
Supplier concentration at certain of our power generation facilities and the inability of suppliers to meet their obligations may expose us to significant financial credit or performance risks.
We may not own the land on which our power generation facilities are located, which could result in disruption to our operations.
Changes in U.S. trade policy and the impact of tariffs could adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial position.
Past performance by members of our management team, our directors or their respective affiliates may not be indicative of our future performance or an investment in us.
Our operations are subject to operational hazards and inherent risks, some of which are beyond our control, and some of which may not be fully covered by insurance.
Our ability to produce our products economically and in commercial quantities could be impaired if we are unable to acquire adequate supplies of water for our dredging operations.
Failure to maintain effective quality control systems at our mining and production facilities could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and operations.

Given the nature of our proppant production operations, we face a material risk of liability, delays and increased cash costs of production from environmental and industrial accidents and operational breakdowns.
Increased stakeholder and market attention to ESG and conservation matters may adversely impact our business and access to capital.
Our business may suffer if we lose or are unable to attract and retain members of our workforce.

A shortage of skilled labor together with rising labor costs in the excavation industry may further increase operating costs, which could adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.

Inaccuracies in our estimates of sand reserves and resource deposits, or deficiencies in our title to those deposits, could result in our inability to mine the deposits or require us to pay higher than expected costs.

All of our product revenue is currently generated at facilities in West Texas. Any adverse developments at those facilities could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Our business and operations depend on our and our customers' ability to obtain and maintain necessary permits.
Our supply agreements may preclude us from taking advantage of increasing prices for proppant or mitigating the effect of increased operational costs during the term of those contracts.
A proppant production facility closure entails substantial costs, and if we close any of our facilities sooner than anticipated, our results of operations may be adversely affected.
Currently, a majority of our operations are concentrated in the Permian Basin, making us vulnerable to risks associated with operating in a limited geographic area.
paragraphs: There are numerous factors that affect our business and operating results, many of which are beyond our control. The following is a summary of significant factors that might cause our future results to differ materially from those currently expected. The risks described below are not the only risks facing our Company. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also affect our business operations. If any of these risks actually occur, our business, financial position, operating results, cash flows, reserves or our ability to pay our debts and other liabilities could suffer, the trading price and liquidity of our securities could decline and you may lose all or part of your investment in our securities.

Our operations that produce and transport proppant are materially dependent on the levels of activity in oil and natural gas exploration, development and production. More specifically, the demand for the proppant we produce is closely related to the number of oil and natural gas wells completed in geological formations where sand-based proppant is used in fracture treatments. These activity levels are affected by both short- and long-term trends in oil and natural gas prices. Additionally, our distributed power operations are also tied to activity levels in the oil and gas industry, most specifically through levels of spending tied to production, gathering, and treatment activities. In recent years, oil and natural gas prices and, therefore, the level of exploration, development and production activity, have experienced significant volatility.

When oil and natural gas prices decrease, exploration and production companies may reduce their exploration, development, production and well completion activities. During such periods, demand for our products and services, which supply oil and natural gas wells, including our transportation and logistics solutions, may decline, and may lead to a decline in the market price of proppant, if the supply of proppant is not similarly reduced. When demand for proppant increases, there may not be a corresponding increase in the prices for our products or our customers may not increase use of our products, which could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

Worldwide economic, political and military events, including tax, trade and tariff policies of the United States and other countries involved in global energy markets, war, terrorist activity, events in the Middle East and initiatives by OPEC+, have contributed, and are likely to continue to contribute, to oil and natural gas price volatility. For example, the recent events in Venezuela and the ongoing armed conflicts between Russia and Ukraine, unrest in Iran, the continuation of, and the escalation in the severity of, these conflicts has led to extreme regional instability, caused dramatic fluctuations in global financial markets and has increased the level of global economic uncertainty, including uncertainty about world-wide oil supply and demand, which in turn has caused increased volatility in commodity prices. Further, the Houthi movement, which controls parts of Yemen, has targeted and launched numerous attacks on Israeli, American and international commercial marine vessels in the Red Sea as the ships approach the Suez Canal, resulting in many shipping companies re-routing to avoid the region altogether and worsening existing supply chain issues, including delays in supplier deliveries, extended lead times and increased cost of freight, impacts to the shipping of oil and gas, insurance and materials. The potential for conflict with Iran, a major oil producer, the Houthi movement in Yemen or the Hezbollah movement in Lebanon has increased as a result of continued, increasing hostilities in the Middle East.

Additionally, warmer than normal winters in North America and other weather patterns may adversely impact the short-term demand for natural gas and, therefore, demand for our products. Reduction in demand for natural gas to generate electricity could also adversely impact the demand for proppant. In addition, any future decrease in the rate at which oil and natural gas reserves are discovered or developed, whether due to increased governmental regulation, limitations on exploration and drilling activity, technological innovations that result in new processes for oil and natural gas production that do not require proppant or other factors, could adversely affect the demand for our products, even in a stronger oil and natural gas price environment. Moreover, the energy transition to a low carbon economy, increased deployment of renewable power generation, renewable fuels and electric vehicles all have the potential to reduce demand for oil and natural gas and consequently the services we provide. The continued or future occurrence of any of these risks could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

Our business is directly affected by capital spending to explore for, develop and produce oil and natural gas and power in the United States. The oil and natural gas industry is cyclical and historically has experienced periodic downturns in activity. During periods of economic slowdown in one or more of the industries or geographic regions we serve or in the worldwide economy, our customers often reduce their production and capital expenditures by deferring or canceling pending projects, even if such customers are not experiencing financial difficulties. These developments can have an adverse effect on sales of our products and our results of operations.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read together with Item 1, "Business," and the Consolidated Financial Statements and the related notes in Item 8 of this Annual Report. For the purposes of this discussion, references to "Atlas Inc." are to AESI Holdings Inc. (f/k/a Atlas Energy Solutions Inc.) for periods prior to the completion of the Up-C Simplification, and to Atlas Energy Solutions Inc. (f/k/a New Atlas HoldCo Inc.) for periods subsequent to the Up-C Simplification. References to the "Company," "we," "us," "our" and like expressions are to Atlas Inc. together with its subsidiaries.

This discussion contains forward-looking statements as a result of many factors, including those set forth under the section titled "Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" and Item 1A. "Risk Factors," and elsewhere in this Annual Report. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results could differ materially from those discussed in or implied by forward-looking statements. Factors that could cause or contribute to these differences include those discussed below and elsewhere in this Annual Report, particularly in Item 1A. "Risk Factors." We do not undertake any obligation to publicly update any forward-looking statements except as otherwise required by applicable law.

We use Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA Margin, Adjusted Free Cash Flow, Adjusted EBITDA less Capital Expenditures, Adjusted Free Cash Flow Margin, Adjusted EBITDA less Capital Expenditures Margin, Adjusted Free Cash Flow Conversion, Contribution Margin, Maintenance Capital Expenditures and Net Debt herein as non-GAAP measures of our financial performance. For further discussion of Contribution Margin, EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted Free Cash Flow, see the section titled "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" in this Item 7 of this Annual Report. We define various terms to simplify the presentation of information in this Annual Report. All share amounts are presented in thousands.

We are a low-cost producer of high-quality, locally sourced 100 mesh and 40/70 sand used as a proppant during the well completion process. Proppant is necessary to facilitate the recovery of hydrocarbons from oil and natural gas wells. One hundred percent of our sand reserves are located in Texas within the Permian Basin and our operations consist of proppant production and processing facilities, including four facilities near Kermit, Texas (together, the "Kermit facilities"), a fifth facility near Monahans, Texas (the "Monahans facility"), and the OnCore distributed mining network.

We operate a differentiated logistics platform that is designed to increase the efficiency, safety and sustainability of the oil and natural gas industry primarily within the Permian Basin. This includes our fleet of fit-for-purpose trucks, trailers, wellsite equipment, and the Dune Express, an overland conveyor infrastructure solution. We have also begun integrating autonomous driving technologies in certain of our fit-for-purpose trucks, creating the first semi-autonomous oilfield logistics network in an effort to increase our automation of the oil and gas proppant supply chain.

We also provide distributed power solutions through a fleet of natural gas-powered reciprocating generators primarily supporting production and artificial lift operations across major United States resource basins. Our generators are designed for heavy-duty, harsh environments for mission critical power needs. Our in-house manufacturing and remanufacturing capabilities, coupled with critical in-field service, provide quality control and standardization across the fleet ensuring market-leading uptime.

The predecessor of Atlas Inc. consists of Atlas LLC and certain of its wholly-owned subsidiaries: Atlas Sand Employee Holding Company, LLC; Atlas Sand Employee Company, LLC; Atlas OLC Employee Company, LLC; Atlas Construction Employee Company, LLC; Fountainhead Logistics Employee Company, LLC; Atlas Sand Construction, LLC; OLC Kermit, LLC; OLC Monahans, LLC; and Fountainhead Logistics, LLC on a consolidated basis (all of which we refer to collectively as "Atlas Predecessor"). Historical periods for Atlas Predecessor are presented on a consolidated basis given the common control ownership. Unless otherwise indicated, the historical consolidated financial information included in this Annual Report presents the historical financial information of Atlas Predecessor. Historical consolidated financial information is not indicative of the results that may be expected in any future periods.

On November 2, 2025, Atlas LLC entered into a reservation agreement (the "Reservation Agreement") for the manufacture of approximately 240 megawatts of power generation equipment. The aggregate cost of such equipment is approximately $278.3 million. The Reservation Agreement was assigned to Stonebriar in connection with entry into the Lease Documents. The cost of the investment will be financed under the Lease Documents as progress payments become due. We expect deliveries to begin in late-2026. Pursuant to the Reservation Agreement, the parties agreed to negotiate and enter into an engineering, procurement and construction agreement governing the terms of the manufacture, delivery and installation of the equipment, which is expected to contain customary representations, warranties and agreements of the parties, indemnification obligations and other customary terms and conditions associated therewith. The Reservation Agreement and terms and conditions of sale also contain customary agreements of the parties and customary terms and conditions.

On July 28, 2025, Atlas LLC entered into the PropFlow Purchase Agreement with BCA HoldCo and certain other signatories thereto, pursuant to which Atlas LLC acquired 100% of the membership interests in PropFlow, and its wholly owned subsidiaries, for approximately $25.0 million in cash, subject to customary post-closing adjustments. In addition, up to $15.0 million in the aggregate in contingent earn-out consideration may be paid to BCA HoldCo in fiscal years 2027 and 2028 pursuant to the PropFlow Purchase Agreement, subject to the achievement of certain revenue targets. Pursuant to the PropFlow Purchase Agreement, Atlas acquired PropFlow's patented on-wellsite proppant filtration technology. The Company borrowed $25.0 million under the 2023 ABL Credit Facility to fund the cash consideration for the PropFlow Acquisition. Additional information on these transactions can be found in Note 3 - Acquisitions of the Financial Statements included elsewhere in this Annual Report.

On February 24, 2025, the Company completed the Moser Acquisition pursuant to the Moser Purchase Agreement by and among Wyatt Holdings, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company and an indirectly wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company (the "Purchaser"), Moser Holdings, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the "Seller"), and for the limited purposes set forth therein, the Company (together with the Purchaser and the Seller, the "Parties"), pursuant to which the Purchaser acquired (i) 100% of the authorized, issued and outstanding equity ownership interests in Moser AcquisitionCo, and (ii) Moser Engine Service, Inc. (d/b/a Moser Energy Systems), a Wyoming corporation and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Moser AcquisitionCo.

Under the terms and conditions of the Moser Purchase Agreement, the aggregate consideration paid to the Seller in the Moser Acquisition consisted of (i) $180.0 million in cash and (ii) approximately 1.7 million shares of Common Stock, issued at the closing of the Moser Acquisition. The Moser Consideration is subject to customary post-closing adjustments. Additional information on these transactions can be found in Note 3 - Acquisitions of the Financial Statements included elsewhere in this Annual Report.

On February 3, 2025, the Company conducted an underwritten public offering of 11.5 million shares of our Common Stock at a public offering price of $23.00 per share (the "Equity Offering"). The Company received approximately $253.1 million of net proceeds from the sale of shares of our Common Stock, after deducting underwriting discounts and commissions. We used the net proceeds from the Equity Offering (i) to repay the $70.0 million outstanding on the 2023 ABL Credit Facility, (ii) to repay $101.3 million of the Deferred Cash Consideration Note, and (iii) the remainder for general corporate purposes.

On February 24, 2025, the Company entered into the Moser Registration Rights Agreement with the Seller that provides, among other things, that the Company will, no later than (a) March 26, 2025, or (b) if the Company is and continues to be a "Well-Known Seasoned Issuer" as defined in Rule 405 of the Securities Act, May 25, 2025, file with the SEC a registration statement registering for resale the Common Stock comprising the Moser Stock Consideration that was issued in connection with the Moser Acquisition, subject to the full or partial exercise of the Moser Stock Consideration subject to redemption by the Company. Pursuant to the Moser Purchase Agreement, the Seller agreed not to lend, offer, sell, contract to sell, sell any option or contract to purchase, purchase any option or contract to sell, grant any option, right, or warrant to purchase, or otherwise transfer or dispose of, any of their shares of Common Stock for a period of 90 days following the closing of the Moser Acquisition, subject to certain exceptions. The Company also agreed to pay certain expenses of the parties incurred in connection with the exercise of their rights under the Moser Registration Rights Agreement, and to indemnify them for certain securities law matters in connection with any registration statement filed pursuant thereto.

During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company repurchased 16,380 shares of Common Stock through open-market purchases under the share repurchase program, at an average price, including commission, of $12.21 per share, for an aggregate purchase price of $200,000. As of December 31, 2025, $199.8 million remains available under the share repurchase program.

paragraphs: Atlas Energy Solutions Inc. 為一間領先的壓裂砂生產商、物流服務及分散式電力解決方案供應商，主要服務美國德克薩斯州西部與紐墨西哥州的佩恩盆地。我們透過兩個應報告分部進行業務運作：砂與物流及電力。我們的使命為提升人類對推動我們生活的石化產品之存取，並透過此方式，為股東創造最大價值。為股東創造價值為我們的根本目標。為實現我們的使命並為股東創造價值，我們致力於為我們的廣泛利害關係人，包括員工及我們運作的社區，優化結果。我們為自己感到自豪的是，我們在石化產業的創新方法驅動了效率，為股東創造價值，同時也帶來區別化的社會與環境進步。本公司已推動創新，以提供業界領先的環境效益，透過減少能源消耗、排放及我們的空中足跡。我們稱此為永續環境與社會進步，並由股東價值創造所驅動。

我們於 2017 年由 Ben M. "Bud" Brigham，我們的執行董事長所創立，並由一羣創業團隊領導，該團隊有建設性顛覆的歷史，為此企業帶來顯著且互補的經驗，包括長期 E&P 運營商的觀點，這提供了對我們產品與服務終端用戶的更高理解。我們的執行管理團隊有經過驗證的紀錄，有產生正向回報與價值創造的歷史。我們作為 E&P 運營商的經驗，對我們理解佩恩盆地內盆地內砂生產與供應所創造的機會至關重要，我們視其為北美首屈一指的頁巖資源，並相信其將在經濟週期中持續保持最活躍。

我們在佩恩盆地運作 14 個壓裂砂生產設施，包括大型的盆地內設施與較小的分散式採礦單位。我們是各種高品質、本地來源壓裂砂的低成本生產商，用於油井完井過程。我們提供乾砂與濕砂，並提供各種篩網尺寸，包括 100 篩網與 40/70 篩網。壓裂砂是關鍵零組件，用以促進從石油與天然氣井中回收石化產品。我們運作一個差異化的物流平台，設計用以提高石油與天然氣產業的效率、安全性與永續性，主要在佩恩盆地內。這包括我們的符合用途的卡車、拖車、井場設備，以及 42 英里長的 Dune Express 搬運系統（全球唯一的壓裂砂搬運系統，也是美國最長的搬運系統）。我們也正在整合自動駕駛技術於部分符合用途的卡車中，創造首個半自動化的石油採礦物流網路，以提高石油與天然氣壓裂砂供應鏈的自動化程度。
我們透過一隊天然氣動力的往復式發電機提供分散式電力解決方案，主要支持美國主要資源盆地的生產與人工抽油作業。我們的發電機設計用以在嚴苛環境中運作，以應對關鍵任務的電力需求。我們的內部製造與再製造能力，搭配關鍵的現場服務，確保整支艦隊的品質控制與標準化，確保市場領先的運轉時間。

我們的 Kermit 設施、Monahans 設施及 OnCore 分散式採礦網路位於德克薩斯州西部。Kermit 設施包括兩個內部開發的 Kermit 設施（"K1/K2"）與兩個在 Hi-Crush 交易中取得的設施（"K115/874"）。這些設施與 OnCore 分散式採礦網路總計擁有 45,855 總計英畝的土地，我們擁有或租賃。我們在 Monahans 有大量非沙丘土地，未包含在我們的儲備或資源估計中，但可在我們移除材料（如土壤與無用的砂）後進行採礦，這些材料位於可用砂之上，必須移除以挖掘可用砂，我們稱之為 "overburden."
Dune Express 起點為我們的 Kermit 設施，延伸至北方德克薩斯盆地中部，為全球首條長距離壓裂砂搬運系統。Dune Express 長度為 42 英里，每年可運輸 13 百萬噸壓裂砂，並 strategically 位於北方德克薩斯盆地，以交付壓裂砂。Dune Express 降低了傳統運輸需求，並提高安全性，透過將卡車從公共道路上移除，減少該地區的交通、事故與致命傷。
我們安裝了兩個永久裝載設施，一個位於德克薩斯州與紐墨西哥州州界中點附近，另一個位於 Dune Express 右側道路末端的 BLM 土地附近，靠近 Lea-Eddy 縣界。搬運系統也使用一個或多個移動卸載系統，可隨時移動與重新定位，以最大化對靠近搬運系統但不靠近任一永久裝載設施的客戶的交付效率。
我們的分散式電力解決方案包括超過 1,000 臺天然氣動力的往復式發電機，主要支持美國主要資源盆地的生產與人工抽油作業。

2025年11月2日，Atlas LLC與某方簽訂保留協議（"保留協議"），用以製造約240 megawatts的電力發電設備。此等設備總成本約為278.3 百萬美元。該保留協議已轉讓予Stonebriar，係因簽訂租賃文件。該投資成本將透過租賃文件以進度款項到期時進行融資。我們預期設備交付將於2026年底開始。根據保留協議，雙方同意協商並簽訂工程、採購與建設協議，規範設備製造、交付與安裝的條款，該協議預期將包含雙方慣常的聲明、保證與協議、賠償義務及其他慣常的條款與條件。
以下地圖顯示截至2025年12月31日，我們營運據點的所在地點：Sand and Logistics

Kermit廠區與Monahans廠區係為生產高品質40/70-mesh與100-mesh砂而建，這些砂廣泛用於Permian Basin上游作業。創新廠區設計與大規模作業有助於降低作業成本並確保現場持續運作。我們的廠區設計有備用系統，以消除可能幹擾生產流程的單一故障點，確保壓裂砂生產與交付的最大可靠性。廠區可全年運作，並具備先進的安全設計、現場用水供應、電力基礎建設及透過聯邦天然氣管線連接的低成本天然氣供應。我們的OnCore分散式採礦網路由9座專為用途設計的移動式處理廠組成，這些廠區可從租賃或客戶所有土地生產濕式（即未乾燥或潮濕）100-mesh砂。在每個OnCore廠區，我們負責採礦與處理原始砂，銷售完成的壓裂砂產品，並復原受擾土地。OnCore廠區的移動性提供了大規模固定廠區採礦作業所無法提供的高度靈活性。

此外，我們受益於廠區的戰略位置，位於Winkler Sand Trend南端與北端的主要高速公路附近。Kermit廠區被兩條州際公路分隔，而Monahans廠區則鄰近兩條公路，其中一條為Interstate 20，有助於將壓裂砂高效運輸至Permian Basin內各處的客戶。OnCore礦區的西部廠區可透過德克薩斯州公路TX-302或美國國道285進入；而東部廠區的主要進口則為Interstate 20、州際公路TX-137、TX-176或TX-349。
我們的砂廠運作由位於德克薩斯州奧斯汀的指揮中心以高度自動化方式進行管理與監控。遠端生態系統使我們的員工可同時管理所有廠區的作業流程，進而提升人力生產力。
我們的差異化物流平台主要運作於Permian Basin。這包括我們的專為用途設計的卡車、拖車、井場設備，以及42英里長的Dune Express輸送系統。

paragraphs: 下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析應與本年度報告第 1 項「業務」、合併財務報表及相關附註，以及第 8 項所述內容一併閱讀。為此討論之目的，提及「Atlas Inc.」時，於 Up-C 簡化完成前，指 AESI Holdings Inc.（原為 Atlas Energy Solutions Inc.），於 Up-C 簡化完成後，指 Atlas Energy Solutions Inc.（原為 New Atlas HoldCo Inc.）。提及「本公司」、「我們」、「我們」、「我們」及類似表達方式時，均指 Atlas Inc. 連同其子公司。
本討論包含許多因素所導致的向前看聲明，包括於「向前看聲明之警示聲明」及第 1A 項「風險因素」中所列舉的內容，以及本年度報告其他部分。這些聲明是基於目前的預期與假設，而這些預期與假設受到風險與不確定性影響。實際結果可能與向前看聲明中所討論或暗示的結果有重大差異。導致這些差異的因素包括下文及本年度報告其他部分所討論的內容，特別是在第 1A 項「風險因素」中。

我們在此使用調整後 EBITDA、調整後 EBITDA 毛利率、調整後自由現金流、調整後 EBITDA 減去資本支出、調整後自由現金流毛利率、調整後 EBITDA 減去資本支出毛利率、調整後自由現金流轉換率、貢獻毛利、維護資本支出及淨負債作為非 GAAP 會計準則衡量我們財務表現的指標。有關貢獻毛利、EBITDA、調整後 EBITDA 及調整後自由現金流的進一步討論，請參閱本年度報告第 7 項「非 GAAP 財務指標」部分。我們定義各種術語以簡化本年度報告中資訊的呈現。所有股數均以千為單位表示。

我們是高品質、本地來源 100 網目及 40/70 砂的低成本生產者，此種砂用作油井及天然氣井完井過程中的壓裂支撐劑。壓裂支撐劑是用來促進從油井及天然氣井中回收石化產品的必要材料。我們 100% 的砂儲備位於德克薩斯州的 Permian Basin，我們的業務包括壓裂支撐劑的生產與加工設施，包括四座位於德克薩斯州 Kermit 的設施（合稱為「Kermit 設施」），以及一座位於德克薩斯州 Monahans 的設施（稱為「Monahans 設施」），以及 OnCore 分散式採礦網路。
我們運營一個差異化的物流平台，旨在提高石油與天然氣產業的效率、安全與永續性，主要在 Permian Basin 區域。這包括我們的適應用途的卡車、拖車、井場設備，以及 Dune Express，一種陸上運輸帶基礎設施解決方案。我們也開始在部分適應用途的卡車中整合自動駕駛技術，建立首個半自動化的石油與天然氣壓裂支撐劑供應鏈物流網路，以提高我們在石油與天然氣壓裂支撐劑供應鏈的自動化程度。
我們也透過一隊天然氣動力的往復式發電機提供分散式電力解決方案，主要支援美國主要石化資源盆地的生產與人工抽油作業。我們的發電機設計用於重負荷、惡劣環境，以應對關鍵任務的電力需求。我們的內部製造與再製造能力，搭配關鍵場地服務，確保整體發電機隊的品質控制與標準化，提供市場領先的運轉時間。

Atlas Inc. 的前身包括 Atlas LLC 及其部分 wholly-owned 子公司：Atlas Sand Employee Holding Company, LLC；Atlas Sand Employee Company, LLC；Atlas OLC Employee Company, LLC；Atlas Construction Employee Company, LLC；Fountainhead Logistics Employee Company, LLC；Atlas Sand Construction, LLC；OLC Kermit, LLC；OLC Monahans, LLC；以及 Fountainhead Logistics, LLC，以合併財務報表方式呈現（以下統稱為「Atlas 前身」）。Atlas 前身的歷史期間以合併財務報表方式呈現，因共同控制權所有。除非另有說明，本年度報告中包含的歷史合併財務資訊呈現 Atlas 前身的歷史財務資訊。歷史合併財務資訊並不代表未來任何期間可能的結果。

2025 年 11 月 2 日，Atlas LLC 與某方簽訂製造約 240 兆瓦電力發電設備的預留協議（稱為「預留協議」）。該設備總成本約為 278.3 百萬美元。預留協議已轉讓至 Stonebriar，以配合簽訂租賃文件。該投資成本將根據租賃文件中進度付款到期時的條件進行融資。我們預期於 2026 年年底開始交付。根據預留協議，雙方同意協商並簽訂工程、採購與建設協議，以規範設備的製造、交付與安裝條件，預期該協議將包含雙方常見的聲明、保證與協議、賠償義務及其他常見的條款與條件。預留協議及銷售條款與條件也包含雙方常見的協議與常見的條款與條件。

於 2025 年 7 月 28 日，Atlas LLC 與 BCA HoldCo 及其他簽約方簽訂 PropFlow 購買協議，根據該協議，Atlas LLC 以約 25.0 百萬美元現金取得 PropFlow 100% 的有限合夥權益，以及其全資子公司，並根據常規的交割後調整條款。此外，根據 PropFlow 購買協議，最多可能於 2027 財年及 2028 財年支付總計 15.0 百萬美元的附條件 earn-out 考慮金，前提是達成特定的營業收入目標。根據 PropFlow 購買協議，Atlas 取得了 PropFlow 的專利油井現場壓裂劑過濾技術。本公司透過 2023 年 ABL 信用融資借款 25.0 百萬美元，以資資金購入 PropFlow 的現金對價。有關這些交易的額外資訊，請參閱本年度報告中其他處所附的財務明細表之附註 3 - 收購事項。

於 2025 年 2 月 24 日，本公司根據 Moser 購買協議完成 Moser 收購，該協議由 Wyatt Holdings, LLC（一家 Delaware 有限責任公司，為本公司間接全資子公司）（稱為「買方」）、Moser Holdings, LLC（一家 Delaware 有限責任公司）（稱為「賣方」），以及為該協議中所規定之有限目的，本公司（與買方及賣方合稱為「各方」）簽訂，根據該協議，買方取得（i）Moser AcquisitionCo 全部已發行及在外流通的股東權益，以及（ii）Moser Engine Service, Inc.（d/b/a Moser Energy Systems），一家 Wyoming 公司，為 Moser AcquisitionCo 的全資子公司。

於 2025 年 2 月 3 日，本公司進行了經認購的公開發行，發行 11.5 百萬股我們的普通股，發行價格為每股 23.00 美元（"權益發行"）。本公司從普通股發行中收到約 253.1 百萬美元的淨資金，扣除經紀折扣及佣金後。我們將權益發行的淨資金（i）用以償還 2023 年 ABL 信用融資約 70.0 百萬美元的貸款餘額，（ii）用以償還 101.3 百萬美元的遞延現金對價憑證，以及（iii）餘額用於一般企業用途。

於 2025 年 2 月 24 日，本公司與賣方簽訂 Moser 登記權協議，根據該協議，本公司同意在（a）2025 年 3 月 26 日前，或（b）若本公司為「知名成熟發行者」（根據證券法第 405 條例定義）則為 2025 年 5 月 25 日前，向 SEC 提交註冊申報書，以登記出售 Moser 收購中發行的普通股，該普通股為 Moser 股票對價的一部分，並根據 Moser 股票對價的全部或部分行使權，以及本公司可能的贖回權。根據 Moser 購買協議，賣方同意在 Moser 收購交割後 90 日內，不得貸款、提供、出售、訂立出售契約、出售任何選擇權或契約購買權、購買任何選擇權或契約出售權、授予任何選擇權、權利或權證，或以其他方式轉讓或處分其普通股，但根據某些例外情況除外。本公司亦同意支付與其根據 Moser 登記權協議行使權利相關的各方費用，並就根據該協議提交的任何註冊申報書所涉及的證券法事項進行賠償。
在 2025 年 12 月 31 日為止的會計年度內，本公司透過公開市場買回 16,380 股普通股，根據股份買回計劃，平均價格（包括佣金）為 12.21 美元每股，總買回價格為 200,000 美元。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，股份買回計劃尚有 199.8 百萬美元可用。

headings: 與本公司業務及營運相關之風險
本公司之業務營運取決於油氣產業之活動程度，而該產業經驗到相當大的波動性。
本公司業務受客戶業務週期性及油氣與電力產業之影響。
對壓裂支撐劑需求減少或開發出技術上及成本上具競爭力之替代壓裂支撐劑或取代水力壓裂之新工藝，將對本公司業務造成負面影響。
本公司之廠房、廠地及設備（"PP&E"）帳面價值可能因減損費用而受影響。
本公司分散式電力業務依賴其與關鍵供應商之關係以取得業務所需之設備。
本公司許多電力系統涉及長銷售週期。
本公司客戶可能不會持續將其電力系統需求委外處理。
分散式電力解決方案在某些應用場合與接取電網的方案競爭。
我們預期我們的電力應報告分部未來將面臨顯著的競爭，因行動電力產業正在演化。
電力發電設施的運營涉及電力產業慣常的重大風險與危險，我們無法保證我們的保險將足夠覆蓋。
我們部分電力發電設施的供應商集中度，以及供應商無法履行其義務的情況，可能使我們面臨顯著的財務信用或履約風險。
我們可能不擁有我們電力發電設施所在地的土地，這可能會導致我們營運中斷。
美國貿易政策的變化及關稅的影響可能對我們的業務、營運結果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
我們管理團隊、董事或其各自關聯公司的過去表現，可能無法反映我們未來的表現或對我們的投資。
我們的營運受營運風險與內在風險影響，部分風險超出我們的控制範圍，部分風險可能未被保險完全覆蓋。
本公司製造產品之經濟性及商業規模之能力，若無法取得足夠之水資源用於挖泥作業，將可能受影響。
若無法在礦場及生產設施維持有效之品質控制系統，將可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況及營運產生不利影響。
考量本公司壓裂砂生產作業之性質，我們面臨因環境及工業事故與營運中斷而導致重大賠償責任、延誤及生產成本增加之風險。
投資人與市場對ESG及保育議題之關注度提高，可能對本公司業務及取得資金之能力產生不利影響。
若本公司失去或無法吸引及留住員工，將可能影響本公司業務。
專業技工人力短缺，加上挖掘業之勞動成本上升，可能進一步提高營運成本，進而對本公司業務、營運結果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
本公司對砂礦儲量及資源儲藏之估計不準確，或對該儲藏之權屬存在缺陷，可能導致無法開採該儲藏，或需支付高於預期之成本。
本公司目前所有產品營收均來自德克薩斯州西部之設施。若該設施發生不利情況，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運結果產生不利影響。
本公司之業務與營運依賴本公司及客戶取得並維持必要許可證之能力。
我們之供應契約可能使我們無法利用壓裂支撐劑價格上漲之機會，或緩衝因契約期間運營成本增加所產生之影響。
壓裂支撐劑生產設施關閉將產生重大成本，若我們任何設施提前於預期關閉，將可能對本公司營運成果產生不利影響。
目前，本公司絕大多數營運集中於帕默斯盆地，使本公司面臨於有限地理區域營運所產生之風險。
paragraphs: 影響本公司營運成果的因素非常多，許多因素為本公司所無法控制。以下為可能導致未來營運成果與目前預期有重大差異的重要因素總結。上述風險並非本公司唯一面臨的風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前本公司尚未知悉或認為不重要，也可能影響本公司營運。若上述任何風險實際發生，將可能使本公司營業、財務狀況、營運成果、現金流、儲備或償還債務及其他負債的能力受損，本公司證券的交易價格與流動性可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資於本公司證券的金額。
本公司生產與運輸壓裂支撐劑的業務，與油氣探勘、開發與生產活動的水準有密切關聯。更明確地說，我們所生產壓裂支撐劑的需求與在使用砂基壓裂支撐劑進行裂縫處理的地質層中完成的油氣井數量密切相關。這些活動水準受短、長期油氣價格趨勢的影響。此外，本公司分散式電力業務也與油氣產業活動水準相關，特別是與與生產、集輸與處理活動相關的支出水準。近年來，油氣價格與因此產生的探勘、開發與生產活動水準，經歷了顯著的波動。
當油氣價格下降時，探勘與生產公司可能會減少其探勘、開發、生產與井完井活動。在這些期間，我們產品與服務的需求，包括我們的運輸與物流解決方案，可能會下降，且若壓裂支撐劑供應未相應減少，壓裂支撐劑的市場價格也可能下降。當壓裂支撐劑需求增加時，我們的產品價格可能不會相應提高，或客戶可能不會增加使用我們的產品，這可能會對本公司營業、財務狀況與營運成果產生不利影響。

全球經濟、政治與軍事事件，包括美國及其他參與全球能源市場國家的稅收、貿易與關稅政策、戰爭、恐怖活動、中東地區事件以及OPEC+的行動，已導致並可能繼續導致油氣價格波動。例如，委內瑞拉近期事件與俄羅斯與烏克蘭之間持續的軍事衝突、伊朗的動盪、這些衝突的持續與嚴重程度升級，導致區域極度不穩定，造成全球金融市場大幅波動，並增加全球經濟不確定性，包括對全球油氣供需的不確定性，進而導致商品價格波動增加。此外，控制也門部分地區的哈迪運動（Houthi movement）已針對以色列、美國與國際商業商船在紅海的船隻發動多次攻擊，當這些船隻接近蘇伊士運河時，導致許多船運公司重新規劃航線以避免該區域，使現有的供應鏈問題更加嚴重，包括供應商交貨延遲、交貨週期延長與運輸費用增加，影響油氣運輸、保險與材料的運送。

此外，北美及其他地區較為溫暖的冬季與其他天氣模式，可能對天然氣的短期需求產生不利影響，進而影響我們產品的需求。天然氣用於發電的需求減少，也可能對壓裂支撐劑的需求產生不利影響。此外，未來油氣儲備發現或開發速度的下降，無論是因政府規範增加、探勘與鑽井活動限制、技術創新導致新的油氣生產流程不需壓裂支撐劑或其他因素，都可能對我們產品的需求產生不利影響，即使在油氣價格較強勁的環境下。此外，能源轉型至低碳經濟、再生能源發電的擴張、再生能源燃料與電動車的普及，都有潛力減少對油氣的需求，進而減少我們所提供的服務需求。這些風險持續或未來發生，都可能對本公司營業、財務狀況與營運成果產生不利影響。
本公司營運直接受美國探勘、開發與生產油氣與電力的資本支出影響。油氣產業具有週期性，歷來經歷過多次活動低潮。在本公司所服務的產業或地理區域，或全球經濟出現經濟放緩期間，即使這些客戶並未遭遇財務困難，客戶仍可能減少其生產與資本支出，延後或取消待執行的項目。這些發展可能對我們產品的銷售與營運成果產生不利影響。
